warrant_audit.note: Historical audit of every citation that was recorded WRITTEN_CONFIRMED before the returned document arrived. A citation that resolves to nothing is not a weak warrant; it is no warrant. A warrant audit can fail in two directions. WA-01, WA-02 and WA-05 found rules claiming more warrant than they had. WA-03, WA-04 and WA-06 found the opposite: rules the authority HAD confirmed, recorded as proposals because the confirming rule was never read. Both are misstatements of what the authority said. REVISION 3: findings WA-01, WA-02, WA-03 and WA-05 are withdrawn as audit errors. A6 and A7 are real, dated, named-authority decisions in the Kelompok 0 v1.2 ingestion. Only WA-04 (the forbidden phrase, which cited no locus at all) and WA-06 (an under-claimed rule) survive as genuine warrant findings. WA-07 records the method defect that produced the false ones.

paraphrase_contract.authority_source: Owner engineering authoring contract. It exists because E1 requires S02 to be a conversation and E2 rejects a long explanation split between two names — neither is reachable if every line must be a verbatim substring of a source row. The instructional requirement is Bariah's (E1, E2, C4); the AUTHORING MECHANISM below is the owner's, and is recorded as his, not hers.
limits: every substantive line cites at least one controlled row of its own unit
a paraphrase names the row text it paraphrases
a paraphrase may not introduce an obligation, prohibition, approval or legal duty that its cited rows do not carry
no analyst note, reviewer annotation or production marker may appear in a line
a scenario frame that makes no claim carries no source burden but may name only objects its unit's rows name
